L-4738 MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING Between The Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority and Nashville Fire Department and Mayor’s Office of Emergency Management A. Purpose The purpose of this Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) is to facilitate collaboration between the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority (MNAA) and the Nashville Fire Department (NFD), and the Mayor’s Office of Emergency Management (OEM) (collectively AGENCY/AGENCIES). All parties recognize MNAA’s need for qualified emergency personnel and services, along with logistical support to fulfill requirements of ongoing critical incident operations and the ability of AGENCIES to provide said personnel and services. Through the partnership that emerges from this MOU, the organizations agree to work in good faith to accomplish the following: NFD will provide fire protection and medical assistance for victims, including transportation to area hospitals, to the MNAA in accordance with the terms of this agreement. OEM will provide or act as point of contact for equipment and additional manpower to include the Tennessee Emergency Management Agency (TEMA) to the MNAA in accordance with the terms of this agreement. B. Terms of this Agreement |. Effective Date This agreement is made and entered into effective as of the date set forth on the signature page (the “Effective Date”) and shall last for a period of two (2) years from Effective Date. The agreement may be extended by mutual written consent.
2. Request for Assistance The MNAA will request assistance through the designated AGENCY representatives or point of contact. At no time will the MNAA directly deploy AGENCIES. ARCHIVE
As information becomes available, MNAA will provide AGENCIES with desired type and quantity of qualified personnel and/or services needed, as well as the location of the critical emergency incident operation(s).
3. Response to Request Upon notification of such request by the MNAA, the designated AGENCY representatives receiving the request shall determine the appropriate type and quantity of personnel and/or support services required. AGENCIES shall activate the necessary member(s) and/or services to fulfill the MNAA request. In the event the needed personnel and/or services are not available, AGENCIES will advise the MNAA requestor of such fact immediately.
4. Deployment Time Frame AGENCY agrees to make every effort in good faith to fulfill the request(s) within a reasonable time period.
5. Command/Access Control The MNAA shall maintain the organization and direction of all crisis management operations involving the airport jurisdictions as outlined in the Metropolitan Nashville and Davidson County Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan. Under extraordinary conditions/events, MNAA and AGENCIES will use the unified command system to facilitate necessary operations. AGENCY personnel are to be considered emergency volunteers during deployment periods. By enacting this MOU, AGENCIES agree to successfully complete the MNAA identification process, as necessary, and thereby obtain MNAA access media which will be displayed when operating on airport property.
6. Practice AGENCY personnel deployed under this agreement may practice within and only within the confines established by documented AGENCY policies, procedures AGENCIES are responsible for making available practice guidelines in the form of AGENCY established protocols as well as patient and/or client documentation / forms. AGENCY is responsible for immediately notifying designated MNAA personnel of any changes in established AGENCY protocols.
2. Liability AGENCIES retain all liability for the actions or inactions of AGENCY and its personnel deployed under this agreement, and for any cause of action or claim arising from AGENCY’S actions or inactions, and such personnel are not and shall not be considered employees of MNAA.
8. HIPAA Compliance To the extent AGENCIES have access to protected health information in the course of performance pursuant to this agreement, AGENCIES will comply with all obligations and requirements of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) and its accompanying regulations, ARCHIVE
9. Compensation The assistance extended under this agreement and any operational plans adopted pursuant to it shall be without reimbursement. 10. ‘eement Not Exclusive This agreement is not intended to be exclusive between the parties hereto. Any of the parties hereto may, as they deem necessary or expedient, enter into separate agreements with any other party or parties. Entry into such separate agreement shall not, unless specifically stated therein, affect any relationship or covenant herein contained. Termination of Agreement Either party may terminate its participation in this agreement by providing written notice 30 working days notice prior to the intended termination date. Termination of said agreement shall not in any way affect the establishment of future collaborations between involved parties.
12. Governing Law This agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Tennessee, and any action between the parties arising from this agreement shall be maintained in the courts of Davidson County, Tennessee.
13. All Legal Provisions Included The parties intend and agree that all legal provisions of law that are required to be included in this agreement shall be deemed to be included. If by mistake or otherwise some provision is not included or is not included in its proper form, then either party may apply to amend the agreement to comply strictly with the law and without prejudice to the rights of either party. Insurance The Metropolitan Government of Davidson County is self-insured for most potential losses. The Code of Laws of the Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County Tennessee provides in Article | Section 2.40.100 that the metropolitan attorney is authorized to settle any property damage claim against the metropolitan government for an amount not in excess of fifteen thousand dollars, and any other type of claim against the metropolitan government for an amount not in excess of five thousand dollars.15. Notices, Approvals, Consents All notices, approvals, consents, demands, requests and other communications required or permitted by this agreement must be in writing to be effective and personally delivered or sent to the addresses set forth below: ARCHIVE
To MNAA: AGENCY: President & CEO Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority 140 BNA Park Drive, Suite 520 Nashville, TN 37214-4114 Department of Public Safety Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority Nashville International Airport 140 BNA Park Drive, Suite 520 Nashville, Tennessee 37214-4114 And to: Nashville Fire Department P.O. Box 196332 Nashville, Tennessee 37219-6332 Mayor’s Office of Emergency Management 2060 15" Avenue South Nashville, Tennessee 37212 ARCHIVE
